rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: When escaping special characters using a meta-character like backslash or ampersand, the meta-character has to be escaped first to avoid double-escaping, and conversely it has to be unescaped last to avoid double-unescaping.
If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.
Allowing writes to arbitrary properties of an object may lead to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
rules.description: A 'for' loop that increments its loop variable but checks it against a lower bound, or decrements its loop variable but checks it against an upper bound, will either stop iterating immediately or keep iterating indefinitely, and is usually indicative of a typo.
An expression that has no effect and is used in a void context is most likely redundant and may indicate a bug.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.
